differences.text: Upstream is controlled-only (value + onChange). The strip owns its value like a native element (D-006): a user selection fires the cancelable tct-value-change and applies the value unless prevented; a controlled framework binding sets `value` back from the event (preventDefault first, or not).

`role="tablist"` is expressed as `pattern="tabs"` (the attribute `role="tablist"` on the element is accepted as the same request). In the tabs pattern the host is the tablist through ElementInternals and the strip renders a div; in the navigation pattern the nav landmark is an inner element (host aria-label / aria-labelledby are delegated to it). The tab items are custom-element children.

The tabs pattern selects on arrow keys by default (APG automatic activation) and offers `activation="manual"` (arrows move focus, Enter or Space select) for panels that are costly to show. Upstream's tablist mode never selects on focus. The navigation pattern stays manual (a link tab must not navigate on focus).

Edge compensation reads the container padding from the private custom properties --_container-padding-inline-start and --_container-padding-inline-end (upstream --container-padding-inline-*, published by Layout containers), like tct-list (LIST-02). Outside a padded container it changes nothing.

The roving tabindex is written on each tab's inner native control, never on the tab host (tabindex=-1 on a shadow host removes its subtree from sequential navigation). A tab list nested in a toolbar keeps its own tab stop (the toolbar's roving skips it).

Tecton tabs are text with a 2px underline in the selected-text ink; rest text is the tab role, hover, keyboard focus and press use the tertiary action fills each paired with its own text role (measured light and dark), and the selected tab keeps its ink over every fill. The scroll arrows are bordered circles with no shadow (Tecton popovers carry a border and no shadow), and the edge fade is a mask (no colour).

differences.text: The menu is the shared tct-dropdown-menu (a slotted tab-styled trigger, a heading and a radio group of options), not a separate popover implementation: it gets the same menu-button behaviour, layer stack and positioning as every other menu.

ArrowDown on the trigger opens the menu (APG menu button), which upstream's TabMenu does not do; with the roving strip this means ArrowDown on the trigger no longer moves to the next stop (arrows Left and Right still do).
